records.source: וַיִּקָּבְצ֧וּ כָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־דָּוִ֖יד חֶבְר֣וֹנָה לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֛ה עַצְמְךָ֥ וּֽבְשָׂרְךָ֖ אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃
records.gloss: And gathered all Israel to David to Hebron, saying, Here, your bone and your flesh [are] we.
pieces: Then all Israel gathered to David in Hebron. "Look," they told him, "we are your own bone and flesh.

L.1: And all Israel gathered to David at Hebron, saying, "Look, we [are] your bone and your flesh.

R.1: Then all Israel came together to David at Hebron. They said, "We are your own relatives.

decisions.choice: 2 Samuel 5:1-3 is the source of verses 1-3: "all Israel gathered" in place of "all the tribes of Israel came"
decisions.reason: Chronicles retells 2 Samuel 5:1-3 almost word for word. Here it says "all Israel gathered to David" where Samuel has "all the tribes of Israel came to David", and "saying" where Samuel has "and said, saying". Chronicles moves straight from Saul's death (chapter 10) to this scene. It leaves out David's seven and a half years as king of Judah alone and the war with Saul's house (2 Samuel 2-4), so the whole nation is seen coming to David at once.

decisions.choice: your bone and your flesh: your own kin, people of the same family
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:1. To be someone's bone and flesh is to be closely related to him (Genesis 2:23; 29:14; Judges 9:2). The people remind David that they belong to the same nation, descended from the same ancestor, Israel.

decisions.choice: your own relatives
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of bone and flesh by its meaning, family kinship, as in 2 Samuel 5:1.

records.heading: David becomes king over all Israel

records.source: גַּם־תְּמ֣וֹל גַּם־שִׁלְשׁ֗וֹם גַּ֚ם בִּהְי֣וֹת שָׁא֣וּל מֶ֔לֶךְ אַתָּ֛ה הַמּוֹצִ֥יא וְהַמֵּבִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ לְךָ֗ אַתָּ֨ה תִרְעֶ֤ה אֶת־עַמִּי֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאַתָּה֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה נָגִ֔יד עַ֖ל עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Even yesterday, even three days ago, even when was Saul king, you [were] the [one] leading out and the [one] bringing in Israel; and said Yahweh your God to you, You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will be ruler over my people Israel.
pieces: In times past, even while Saul reigned, you were the one who led Israel out to battle and brought them back. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God said to you, 'You are the one who will shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel; you will become ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'"

L.2: Even yesterday and the day before, even when Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought [it] in. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God said to you, 'You will shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel, and you will be ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'"

R.2: Even when Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel's army out to fight and brought it home again. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God told you, 'You will be the shepherd of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. You will be the leader of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'"

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:2, with "Yahweh your God" and "ruler over my people Israel"
decisions.reason: The words follow 2 Samuel 5:2 with small differences: Chronicles has "even" three times; it says "when Saul was king" without "over us"; it calls God "Yahweh your God" where Samuel has "Yahweh"; and it has "ruler over my people Israel" where Samuel has "ruler over Israel", so the people are twice called God's own. Chronicles spells the words for "you were the one who led out and brought in" in the ordinary way, without the unusual spelling noted at 2 Samuel 5:2.

decisions.choice: yesterday and three days ago: in the past, for some time now
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:2. The pair of time words is a Hebrew way of saying "before now" (Genesis 31:2; Exodus 5:8). The people mean that David's leadership is nothing new.

decisions.choice: leading out and bringing in: leading the army to war and home again
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:2. To lead out and bring in is said of a commander who takes his men into battle and brings them back (Numbers 27:17; Joshua 14:11; 1 Samuel 18:13, 16).

decisions.choice: shepherd my people; ruler: the king cares for a people that belongs to God
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:2. The verb "shepherd" pictures a king who guards and feeds a flock that is not his own, and "ruler" is the word for a leader appointed by God (1 Samuel 9:16; 13:14). David was taken from the sheep (Psalm 78:70-72).

decisions.choice: out to battle and brought them back (Balanced); led Israel's army out to fight and brought it home again (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:2, Balanced and Readable say what the idiom of going out and coming in refers to, the leading of troops in war.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: Readable says "leader" for the word rendered "ruler", as in the rest of these books.

records.source: וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ כָּל־זִקְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶל־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ חֶבְר֔וֹנָה וַיִּכְרֹת֩ לָהֶ֨ם דָּוִ֥יד בְּרִ֛ית בְּחֶבְר֖וֹן לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּמְשְׁח֨וּ אֶת־דָּוִ֤יד לְמֶ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־שְׁמוּאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And came all [the] elders of Israel to the king to Hebron, and cut for them David a covenant in Hebron before Yahweh; and they anointed David for king over Israel, according to [the] word of Yahweh by [the] hand of Samuel.
pieces: When all the elders of Israel had come to the king in Hebron, David made a covenant with them there in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they anointed David king over Israel, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised through Samuel.

L.3: And all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them at Hebron before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and they anointed David [as] king over Israel, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by the hand of Samuel.

R.3: All the leaders of Israel came to King David at Hebron. There David made a covenant with them in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they poured oil on his head to make him king over Israel. This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said through Samuel.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:3, adding "according to the word of Yahweh by Samuel"
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Samuel 5:3, with "David" where Samuel has "King David". Chronicles adds a closing phrase of its own: the anointing happened according to the word of Yahweh through Samuel. It points back to Samuel's anointing of the young David at God's command (1 Samuel 16:1-13), so that the people's choice is shown to carry out what God had already said.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Samuel: through Samuel, as God's messenger
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" a person means through him, as the one who carries a message or does a task (Exodus 9:35; 1 Kings 12:15).

decisions.choice: made a covenant before Yahweh: a binding agreement between the king and the people, with God as witness
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:3. The verb is literally "cut", the usual word for making a covenant. A covenant between a king and his people set out what each owed the other, under oath (1 Samuel 10:25; 2 Kings 11:17).

decisions.choice: leaders; poured oil on his head to make him king
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:3, Readable says "leaders" for "elders", the senior heads of families and tribes, and explains what anointing is.

decisions.choice: as the LORD had promised through Samuel (Balanced); This was what the LORD had said through Samuel (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "according to the word of the LORD" as a clause, and Readable makes it a sentence of its own.

records.source: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ דָּוִ֧יד וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם הִ֣יא יְב֑וּס וְשָׁם֙ הַיְבוּסִ֔י יֹשְׁבֵ֖י הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And went David and all Israel [to] Jerusalem, it [is] Jebus; and there [were] the Jebusites, [the] inhabitants of the land.
pieces: Then David and all Israel marched on Jerusalem, that is, Jebus, where the Jebusites lived, the people of that land.

L.4: And David and all Israel went [to] Jerusalem, that [is] Jebus; and the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, [were] there.

R.4: Then David and all the Israelites went to attack Jerusalem, which was then called Jebus. The Jebusites lived there.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:6, with "David and all Israel" and "that is, Jebus"
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:6 says "the king and his men" went to Jerusalem, David's own fighting men. Chronicles has "David and all Israel", so the whole nation that has just made him king (verses 1-3) shares in taking the city. It also adds that Jerusalem was then called Jebus, after the Jebusites, as in Joshua 18:28 and Judges 19:10-11.

decisions.choice: the Jebusites: the Canaanite people who still held Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:6. The Jebusites are named among the peoples of Canaan (Genesis 15:21; Deuteronomy 7:1). Neither Judah nor Benjamin had been able to drive them out of Jerusalem (Joshua 15:63; Judges 1:21).

decisions.choice: marched on (Balanced); went to attack (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is simply "went", but "against" the city is plain from the next verses. Balanced and Readable say so, as in 2 Samuel 5:6. Readable says "which was then called" to show that Jebus is the city's old name.

records.heading: David captures Jerusalem

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֤י יְבוּס֙ לְדָוִ֔יד לֹ֥א תָב֖וֹא הֵ֑נָּה וַיִּלְכֹּ֤ד דָּוִיד֙ אֶת־מְצֻדַ֣ת צִיּ֔וֹן הִ֖יא עִ֥יר דָּוִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And said [the] inhabitants of Jebus to David, Not you will come here. And captured David the stronghold of Zion; it [is the] city of David.
pieces: The people of Jebus told David, "You will not get in here." But David captured the stronghold of Zion, which is now the City of David.

L.5: And the inhabitants of Jebus said to David, "You will not come in here." But David captured the stronghold of Zion; that [is] the City of David.

R.5: The people of Jebus said to David, "You will never get inside this city!" But David captured the fortress of Zion. It became known as the City of David.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:6-7, without the taunt about the blind and the lame
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 5:6 the Jebusites boast that even the blind and the lame could keep David out. Chronicles gives only the first words of the boast, "You will not come in here", calls the speakers "the inhabitants of Jebus", and goes straight on to the capture, told in the same words as 2 Samuel 5:7.

decisions.choice: the stronghold of Zion: the fortified hill of the Jebusite city
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:7. Zion was the ridge south of the later temple hill, on which the old city stood. In later books the name comes to mean the whole of Jerusalem, and the place where Yahweh dwells (Psalm 2:6; Isaiah 2:3).

decisions.choice: that is the City of David: a note from the writer's day
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:7, the writer explains the old name by the one his readers knew. Verse 7 tells how the name was given.

decisions.choice: which is now (Balanced); It became known as (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:7, Balanced and Readable show that the name came later. Readable says "fortress" for "stronghold".

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔יד כָּל־מַכֵּ֤ה יְבוּסִי֙ בָּרִ֣אשׁוֹנָ֔ה יִהְיֶ֥ה לְרֹ֖אשׁ וּלְשָׂ֑ר וַיַּ֧עַל בָּרִאשׁוֹנָ֛ה יוֹאָ֥ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֖ה וַיְהִ֥י לְרֹֽאשׁ׃
records.gloss: And said David, Anyone striking a Jebusite at first will be for chief and for commander. And went up at first Joab son of Zeruiah, and he became chief.
pieces: David had said, "Whoever is first to strike down a Jebusite will become chief and commander." Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, so he became chief.

L.6: And David said, "Whoever strikes a Jebusite first will become chief and commander." And Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became chief.

R.6: David had promised, "The first man to attack the Jebusites will become the chief commander." Joab son of Zeruiah was the first to go up, so he became the chief.

decisions.choice: in place of 2 Samuel 5:8: Joab goes up first and becomes chief; no water shaft and no saying about the blind and the lame
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 5:8 David gives an unfinished order about reaching the defenders by the water shaft, and the writer explains a saying about the blind and the lame. Chronicles has neither. It gives instead David's promise of the chief command to the first man to strike the Jebusites, and tells that Joab son of Zeruiah went up first and won it. This may be the promise that the broken sentence in Samuel seems to lack.

decisions.choice: David said: the promise came before the capture told in verse 5
decisions.reason: Verse 5 tells the capture in one short clause; verse 6 goes back to tell how it was done. David's words were spoken before the attack.

decisions.choice: chief and commander: head of David's army
decisions.reason: "Chief" is literally "head", and "commander" is the usual word for an officer. Together they mean the top command of the army, the post Joab holds in 18:15 and 27:34. Joab is already leading David's men in 2 Samuel 2:13; Chronicles tells how his command over the whole army began.

decisions.choice: went up: climbed up into the city on its hill
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stood on a ridge, so attackers "went up" against it. The word may also look to the water shaft of 2 Samuel 5:8, but Chronicles does not say how Joab got in.

decisions.choice: David had said (Balanced); David had promised (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the promise was made before the capture, as m2 explains. Readable puts "chief and commander" as "the chief commander", one post.

records.source: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב דָּוִ֖יד בַּמְצָ֑ד עַל־כֵּ֥ן קָרְאוּ־ל֖וֹ עִ֥יר דָּוִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And dwelt David in the stronghold; therefore they called it [the] city of David.
pieces: David took up residence in the stronghold, and that is why it was called the City of David.

L.7: And David lived in the stronghold; therefore they called it the City of David.

R.7: David made his home in the fortress, so people called it the City of David.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:9a, with "therefore they called it" in place of "and he called it"
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 5:9 David himself names the stronghold. Chronicles says that people called it the City of David because he lived there. Chronicles also uses a shorter form of the word for "stronghold" here, with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: they called: people in general called it
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. "They" means people in general, so the name came from common use.

decisions.choice: it was called
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the verb with no stated subject as a passive; Readable says "people".

records.source: וַיִּ֤בֶן הָעִיר֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב מִן־הַמִּלּ֖וֹא וְעַד־הַסָּבִ֑יב וְיוֹאָ֕ב יְחַיֶּ֖ה אֶת־שְׁאָ֥ר הָעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And he built the city from round about, from the Millo and to the surrounding; and Joab restored [the] rest of the city.
pieces: He built up the city all around, from the Millo to the area around it, and Joab repaired the rest of the city.

L.8: And he built the city all around, from the Millo even to the surrounding [area]; and Joab restored the rest of the city.

R.8: David built up the city all around, from the Millo (a supporting terrace) out to the area around it. Joab repaired the rest of the city.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:9b, adding that Joab repaired the rest of the city
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:9 says that David built "all around, from the Millo and inward". Chronicles says that he built "the city", "from the Millo to the surrounding area", and adds that Joab restored the rest of the city. Joab, now chief (verse 6), shares in the work.

decisions.choice: the Millo: probably a terrace of built-up earth and stone
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:9. The name comes from the verb "to fill", so it probably means a great terrace or rampart of packed earth and stone on the steep slope. Its exact form and place are not known.

decisions.choice: restored: repaired, rebuilt what was damaged
decisions.reason: The verb is "make live". Used of a city or of stones it means to bring back into use what lay ruined (Nehemiah 3:34). Joab repaired the parts of the city not covered by David's own building.

decisions.choice: David; the Millo (a supporting terrace)
decisions.reason: Readable names David as the builder, to keep him apart from Joab, and explains the Millo briefly, as in 2 Samuel 5:9.

records.source: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִ֖יד הָל֣וֹךְ וְגָד֑וֹל וַיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת עִמּֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And went David going and great, and Yahweh of hosts [was] with him.
pieces: David became greater and greater, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies was with him.

L.9: And David went on becoming greater and greater, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [was] with him.

R.9: David became more and more powerful, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies was with him.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:10, with "Yahweh of hosts" in place of "Yahweh, God of hosts"
decisions.reason: Chronicles has the shorter, more usual form of the title, without "God". Otherwise the verse is the same as 2 Samuel 5:10.

decisions.choice: went going and great: grew steadily greater
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:10. The verb "go" with a second verb describes something that keeps on happening (Genesis 26:13; 1 Samuel 2:26).

decisions.choice: Yahweh of hosts was with him: the reason for David's rise
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:10. David's success comes from God's presence (1 Samuel 16:18; 18:14). The title means Yahweh, commander of the armies of heaven and earth (1 Samuel 1:3).

decisions.choice: for, because; the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the second clause gives the reason, and say "Armies" for "hosts", as in the rest of these books.

records.source: וְאֵ֨לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֤י הַגִּבּוֹרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֔יד הַמִּתְחַזְּקִ֨ים עִמּ֧וֹ בְמַלְכוּת֛וֹ עִם־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַמְלִיכ֑וֹ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And these [are the] chiefs of the mighty men who [belonged] to David, the [ones] strengthening themselves with him in his kingdom with all Israel to make him king, according to [the] word of Yahweh concerning Israel.
pieces: These are the chiefs of David's mighty warriors, who gave him strong support in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised concerning Israel.

L.10: And these [are] the chiefs of the mighty men whom David had, who held strongly with him in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning Israel.

R.10: These were the leaders of David's best warriors. Together with all Israel, they gave strong support to his rule and helped make him king. This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised about Israel.

decisions.choice: a heading of Chronicles' own for the list of 2 Samuel 23:8-39
decisions.reason: In Samuel the list of David's warriors stands near the end of his story, after his last words (2 Samuel 23:1-7). Chronicles places it at the start of his reign and gives it this heading, which ties the warriors to his being made king by all Israel (verses 1-3).

decisions.choice: held strongly with him: put their strength behind him, gave him firm support
decisions.reason: The verb is a form of "be strong" that means to show oneself strong; with "with him" it means to stand firmly on someone's side.

decisions.choice: according to the word of Yahweh concerning Israel: the warriors' support carries out God's promise
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats the end of verse 3. The men who made David king did what Yahweh had said about Israel, that David would shepherd his people (verse 2).

decisions.choice: mighty warriors (Balanced); best warriors (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:8: Literal keeps "mighty men", Balanced says "mighty warriors" and Readable "best warriors" through the chapter.

records.heading: David's mighty warriors

records.source: וְאֵ֛לֶּה מִסְפַּ֥ר הַגִּבֹּרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֑יד יָשָׁבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־חַכְמוֹנִ֗י רֹ֚אשׁ הַשָּׁ֣לִישִׁ֔ים הֽוּא־עוֹרֵ֧ר אֶת־חֲנִית֛וֹ עַל־שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת חָלָ֖ל בְּפַ֥עַם אֶחָֽת׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] number of the mighty men who [belonged] to David: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the Thirty; he wielded his spear against three hundred slain at one time.
pieces: This is the roll of David's mighty warriors. Jashobeam son of Hachmoni was chief of the Thirty. He raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them at one time.

L.11: And this [is] the count of the mighty men whom David had: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the Thirty; he wielded his spear against three hundred slain at one time.

R.11: Here is the list of David's best warriors. Jashobeam son of Hachmoni was the leader of the Thirty. In one battle he fought three hundred men with his spear and killed them.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:8, with the name Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, "he wielded his spear", and three hundred in place of eight hundred
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 23:8 names this man Josheb-Basshebeth the Tahchemonite and adds "he was Adino the Eznite" without a verb for the fighting. Chronicles gives the name as Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, the form used for a commander in 27:2, and has "he wielded his spear", which gives a clear sense. It also counts three hundred slain where Samuel has eight hundred; three hundred is also the number for Abishai (verse 20). Samuel's "names" is "count" here.

decisions.choice: chief of the Thirty: the written text; the spoken reading is "chief of the officers"
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew letters give "the Thirty", the group this list names (verses 15, 25, 42). The scribes' marginal reading, to be read aloud, gives "the officers", picked men close to the king, as in 2 Samuel 23:8; its letters can also be read "the Three". Here the written form is followed. Either way Jashobeam heads David's warriors.

decisions.choice: the count: the list, the roll
decisions.reason: The word means a number or count, here the roll of names that follows.

decisions.choice: the Thirty (capital T)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23, where "the Three" or "the Thirty" stands alone as the name of a group of warriors, every level writes it with a capital letter, so the reader can tell the group from the number.

decisions.choice: and killed them
decisions.reason: "Against three hundred slain" means he fought them and they fell by his hand, so Balanced and Readable supply "killed", as in 2 Samuel 23:8, 18.

records.source: וְאַחֲרָ֛יו אֶלְעָזָ֥ר בֶּן־דּוֹד֖וֹ הָאֲחוֹחִ֑י ה֖וּא בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֥ה הַגִּבֹּרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And after him Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite; he [was] among [the] three the mighty men.
pieces: Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite. He was one of the three mighty warriors.

L.12: And after him [was] Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite; he [was] among the three mighty men.

R.12: Next came Eleazar son of Dodo from the clan of Ahoah. He was one of the three best warriors.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:9a, with "the Ahohite" for "son of an Ahohite"
decisions.reason: The words follow 2 Samuel 23:9 up to "the three mighty men". Samuel's next words, about taunting the Philistines, are told differently in verse 13.

decisions.choice: the three mighty men: the Three, who stood above David's other warriors
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 23:8-12 the Three are Josheb-Basshebeth, Eleazar and Shammah. Chronicles names only Jashobeam and Eleazar; Shammah's deed is missing (see verse 13).

decisions.choice: from the clan of Ahoah
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:9, Readable explains "the Ahohite", a man of the family of Ahoah, a descendant of Benjamin (8:4).

records.source: הֽוּא־הָיָ֨ה עִם־דָּוִ֜יד בַּפַּ֣ס דַּמִּ֗ים וְהַפְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ נֶאֱסְפוּ־שָׁ֣םלַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַתְּהִ֛י חֶלְקַ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה מְלֵאָ֣ה שְׂעוֹרִ֑ים וְהָעָ֥ם נָ֖סוּ מִפְּנֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: He was with David at Pas-dammim, and the Philistines were gathered there for battle; and was a plot of the field full [of] barley, and the people fled from before [the] Philistines.
pieces: He was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines had gathered there for battle. There was a plot of land full of barley, and the troops ran from the Philistines.

L.13: He was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines were gathered there for battle, and there was a plot of the field full of barley; and the people fled before [the] Philistines.

R.13: He was with David at Pas-dammim, where the Philistines had gathered for battle. There was a field there full of barley, and the army of Israel ran away from the Philistines.

decisions.choice: in place of 2 Samuel 23:9-11: one story at Pas-dammim, in a field of barley, with Shammah missing
decisions.reason: In Samuel, Eleazar's fight (2 Samuel 23:9-10) and Shammah's stand in a field of lentils (23:11-12) are two separate deeds. Chronicles has one story: Eleazar is with David at Pas-dammim, and the field is full of barley, not lentils. Shammah son of Agee is not named, though he would be the third of the Three. A copyist's eye may have jumped from one "the Philistines gathered" to the next, leaving out the end of Eleazar's story and the start of Shammah's.

decisions.choice: Pas-dammim: the Ephes-dammim of 1 Samuel 17:1
decisions.reason: Pas-dammim is a shorter form of Ephes-dammim, where the Philistines camped when David fought Goliath (1 Samuel 17:1). 2 Samuel 23:9 has "when they taunted" in its place.

decisions.choice: a plot full of barley: a crop the Philistines had come to plunder
decisions.reason: Barley was the first grain to ripen in spring (Ruth 1:22). Raiders often came at harvest to take the crops (Judges 6:3-4), so the men were defending their people's food.

decisions.choice: the people (Literal); the troops (Balanced); the army of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:11, "the people" here is Israel's army.

records.source: וַיִּֽתְיַצְּב֤וּ בְתוֹךְ־הַחֶלְקָה֙ וַיַּצִּיל֔וּהָ וַיַּכּ֖וּ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיּ֥וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֖ה תְּשׁוּעָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they took their stand in [the] middle of the plot and delivered it, and struck down [the] Philistines; and saved Yahweh [with] a salvation great.
pieces: But they took their stand in the middle of the plot, defended it and struck down the Philistines, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved them with a great victory.

L.14: And they took their stand in [the] middle of the plot and rescued it and struck down [the] Philistines; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved [them with] a great victory.

R.14: But David and Eleazar stood in the middle of the field and kept the Philistines from taking it. They killed the Philistines, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rescued Israel with a great victory.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:12, with the verbs in the plural and "Yahweh saved with a great victory"
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 23:12 the verbs are singular, for Shammah alone. Chronicles has the plural, since David and Eleazar are both in the field (verse 13). Samuel says Yahweh "worked a great victory"; Chronicles says Yahweh "saved", using the verb that belongs with the noun for victory or salvation.

decisions.choice: they: David and Eleazar
decisions.reason: Verse 13 places Eleazar with David at Pas-dammim, so the plural verbs refer to the two of them, standing together when the army fled.

decisions.choice: Yahweh saved with a great victory: the victory is God's, though the men fought
decisions.reason: The noun means rescue or deliverance, here won in battle. The narrator credits it to Yahweh, as in 2 Samuel 23:10, 12 and 1 Samuel 14:6.

decisions.choice: saved them (Balanced); rescued Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb has no object in the Hebrew. Balanced and Readable supply the people saved, and Readable names David and Eleazar as m2 explains.

records.source: וַיֵּרְד֡וּ שְֽׁלוֹשָׁה֩ מִן־הַשְּׁלוֹשִׁ֨ים רֹ֤אשׁ עַל־הַצֻּר֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔יד אֶל־מְעָרַ֖ת עֲדֻלָּ֑ם וּמַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים חֹנָ֖ה בְּעֵ֥מֶק רְפָאִֽים׃
records.gloss: And went down three of the thirty chief to the rock to David to [the] cave of Adullam; and [the] camp of [the] Philistines [was] encamping in [the] Valley of Rephaim.
pieces: Once three chief men of the Thirty went down to the rock, to join David at the cave of Adullam, while an army of Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.

L.15: And three of the Thirty, chiefs, went down to the rock, to David, to the cave of Adullam, and the camp of [the] Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.

R.15: One time three leaders from the Thirty went down to the rocks where David was, at the cave of Adullam. An army of Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:13, with "to the rock" in place of "at harvest", and "camp" in place of "troop"
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 23:13 says the three came "at harvest"; Chronicles has "to the rock", and the two Hebrew words look alike. Chronicles also says "the camp of the Philistines" where Samuel has "a troop of Philistines", and it writes "three" plainly where the written text of Samuel has "thirty".

decisions.choice: the rock; the cave of Adullam; the Valley of Rephaim
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:13. Adullam lay in the hill country southwest of Bethlehem; David hid in a cave there when he fled from Saul (1 Samuel 22:1). "The rock" is the rocky height where the cave was. The Valley of Rephaim runs southwest from Jerusalem toward Bethlehem (14:9).

decisions.choice: Once, One time
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:13, Balanced and Readable add "once" to show that a new story begins. Readable says "the rocks where David was" to make the place clear.

records.source: וְדָוִ֖יד אָ֣ז בַּמְּצוּדָ֑ה וּנְצִ֣יב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אָ֖ז בְּבֵ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: And David then [was] in the stronghold, and [the] garrison of [the] Philistines then [was] in Bethlehem.
pieces: At that time David was in the stronghold, and a Philistine garrison was then in Bethlehem.

L.16: And David [was] then in the stronghold, and [the] garrison of [the] Philistines [was] then in Bethlehem.

R.16: At that time David was in his hiding place in the hills, and a group of Philistine soldiers was holding Bethlehem.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:14, word for word
decisions.reason: Chronicles gives the verse as Samuel has it, with the word "in" before Bethlehem written out.

decisions.choice: a Philistine garrison in Bethlehem: an enemy post in David's home town
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:14. Bethlehem was David's birthplace (1 Samuel 16:1), and the Philistines held posts inside Israel's land to control it (1 Samuel 13:23).

decisions.choice: his hiding place in the hills
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:14, Readable explains "stronghold", which here is a place of refuge in rough country.

records.source: וַיִּתְאָ֥יו דָּוִ֖יד וַיֹּאמַ֑ר מִ֚י יַשְׁקֵ֣נִי מַ֔יִם מִבּ֥וֹר בֵּֽית־לֶ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּשָּֽׁעַר׃
records.gloss: And longed David and said, Who will give me drink water from [the] well of Bethlehem which [is] at the gate?
pieces: David had a longing and said, "If only someone would get me water to drink from Bethlehem's well, the one by the gate!"

L.17: And David longed and said, "Who will give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that [is] by the gate?"

R.17: David felt homesick and said, "I wish someone would bring me water from the well by Bethlehem's gate!"

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:15, word for word
decisions.reason: Chronicles gives David's words as Samuel has them. The written letters of the verb "longed" differ slightly from the spoken reading, with no change of sense.

decisions.choice: who will give me water to drink? a wish, not a command
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:15. "Who will ...?" is a common Hebrew way of saying "if only" (Numbers 11:4). David speaks of a longing; he does not order anyone to go.

decisions.choice: If only someone would (Balanced); I wish someone would (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:15, Balanced and Readable turn the question into the wish it expresses, and Readable says "homesick" for "longed".

records.source: וַיִּבְקְע֨וּ הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֜ה בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיִּֽשְׁאֲבוּ־מַ֨יִם֙ מִבּ֤וֹר בֵּֽית־לֶ֨חֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשַּׁ֔עַר וַיִּשְׂא֖וּ וַיָּבִ֣אוּ אֶל־דָּוִ֑יד וְלֹֽא־אָבָ֤ה דָוִיד֙ לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֔ם וַיְנַסֵּ֥ךְ אֹתָ֖ם לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And broke through the three into [the] camp of [the] Philistines, and drew water from [the] well of Bethlehem which [was] at the gate, and carried and brought to David; and not was willing David to drink them, and he poured them out to Yahweh.
pieces: So the three men broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well of Bethlehem by the gate, and carried it back to David. But David would not drink it. Instead he poured it out as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.18: And the three broke through into the camp of [the] Philistines and drew water from the well of Bethlehem that [was] by the gate, and carried [it] and brought [it] to David. But David was not willing to drink it, and he poured it out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.18: So the three men forced their way through the Philistine camp. They got water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem and carried it back to David. But David refused to drink it. Instead he poured it out on the ground as a gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:16, with "the three" and "David" named again
decisions.reason: Samuel says "the three mighty men"; Chronicles says simply "the three", the three men of verse 15, and names David again as the one who would not drink.

decisions.choice: poured it out to Yahweh: a drink offering
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:16. The verb is the one used for pouring out a drink offering (Genesis 35:14; Numbers 28:7). David treats the water as too precious for himself and gives it to God.

decisions.choice: the three (small letter)
decisions.reason: "The three" here are the three men of verse 15, not the group called the Three, so every level keeps a small letter. Balanced and Readable add "men".

decisions.choice: as an offering (Balanced); on the ground as a gift (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:16, Balanced and Readable say what pouring out to the LORD was, so it does not read as wasting the water.

records.source: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר חָלִילָה֩ לִּ֨י מֵאֱלֹהַ֜י מֵעֲשׂ֣וֹת זֹ֗את הֲדַ֣ם הָאֲנָשִׁים֩ הָאֵ֨לֶּה אֶשְׁתֶּ֤ה בְנַפְשׁוֹתָם֙ כִּ֣י בְנַפְשׁוֹתָ֣ם הֱבִיא֔וּם וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֑ם אֵ֣לֶּה עָשׂ֔וּ שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת הַגִּבּוֹרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he said, Far be it to me from my God from doing this; the blood of the men these will I drink with their lives? For with their lives they brought it. And not was he willing to drink it. These did [the] three the mighty men.
pieces: He said, "Before my God, far be it from me to do this! Shall I drink the blood of these men who went at the risk of their lives? For they risked their lives to bring it." So he would not drink it. Such were the deeds of the three mighty warriors.

L.19: And he said, "Far be it from me before my God that I should do this! Shall I drink the blood of these men, [who went] at [the risk of] their lives? For at [the risk of] their lives they brought it." And he was not willing to drink it. These [things] the three mighty men did.

R.19: He said, "Before my God, I could never do this! This water is like the blood of these men. They risked their lives to bring it to me." So he would not drink it. These are the brave things the three best warriors did.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:17, with "before my God" and the question completed
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 23:17 David calls on Yahweh by name. Chronicles has "from my God", that is, before God or in his sight. It completes Samuel's short question with "shall I drink" and adds "for at the risk of their lives they brought it".

decisions.choice: far be it from me before my God: a strong refusal, made in God's sight
decisions.reason: The phrase means "it would be a profane thing for me". Saying it before God makes the refusal almost an oath (1 Samuel 24:7; 26:11).

decisions.choice: the blood of these men: the water cost the men their lives at risk, so it is like their blood
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:17. Blood stands for life (Leviticus 17:11), and blood was not to be drunk but poured out (Deuteronomy 12:16). Drinking water bought at the risk of the men's lives would be like drinking their blood.

decisions.choice: [who went] at [the risk of] (Literal); who went at the risk of; risked (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "With their lives" means risking them, so all levels add "risk", as in 2 Samuel 23:17. Readable turns the question into a statement of what it means.

records.source: וְאַבְשַׁ֣י אֲחִֽי־יוֹאָ֗ב ה֤וּאהָיָה֙ רֹ֣אשׁ הַשְּׁלוֹשָׁ֔ה וְהוּא֙ עוֹרֵ֣ר אֶת־חֲנִית֔וֹ עַל־שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת חָלָ֑ל וְלוֹ־שֵׁ֖ם בַּשְּׁלוֹשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And Abishai brother of Joab, he was chief of the three; and he wielded his spear against three hundred slain, and [belonged] to him a name among the three.
pieces: Abishai, the brother of Joab, was chief of the Three. He raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them, and he won a name alongside the Three.

L.20: And Abishai, [the] brother of Joab, he was chief of the Three; and he wielded his spear against three hundred slain, and he had a name among the Three.

R.20: Abishai, the brother of Joab, was the leader of the Three. He fought three hundred men with his spear and killed them. So he became as famous as the Three.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:18, without "son of Zeruiah"
decisions.reason: Chronicles leaves out "son of Zeruiah" after Joab's name; otherwise the verse follows Samuel. Abishai was David's nephew (2:16).

decisions.choice: he had a name: the spoken reading; the written letters give "he had no name"
alternatives: he had no name among the Three
decisions.reason: The written letters read "and not a name among the Three"; the scribes' reading, like 2 Samuel 23:18, gives "and he had a name among the Three". The spoken reading is followed. The written form would mean that he was not counted with the Three, which agrees with verse 21.

decisions.choice: chief of the Three: some witnesses read "the Thirty"
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:18, verse 21 says that Abishai did not reach the Three, so some witnesses read "chief of the Thirty", which gives a clearer sense. The Hebrew "the Three" is followed here.

decisions.choice: the Three (capital T)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:18, the name of the group is written with a capital letter at every level. Balanced and Readable supply "killed", as in verse 11.

records.source: מִן־הַשְּׁלוֹשָׁ֤ה בַשְּׁנַ֨יִם֙ נִכְבָּ֔ד וַיְהִ֥י לָהֶ֖ם לְשָׂ֑ר וְעַד־הַשְּׁלוֹשָׁ֖ה לֹֽא־בָֽא׃ס
records.gloss: Than the three, by two, honored, and he became to them for commander; and to the three not he came.
pieces: He was doubly honored above the Three and became their commander, but he did not reach the rank of the Three.

L.21: Above the Three he was doubly honored, and he became their commander; but to the Three he did not come.

R.21: He was given more honor than the Three and became their commander. But he was never one of the Three.

decisions.choice: above the Three, doubly honored: the sense of "by two" is uncertain
alternatives: of the Three, in the second rank, he was honored
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "from the Three, by two, honored". "By two" may mean "twice over", that is, more highly honored; or "above the two", the other two of a group; or "in the second rank". 2 Samuel 23:19 has instead "was he not honored above the Three?", and the two readings may come from similar letters. The sense followed here agrees with Samuel: Abishai was honored and led others, but did not rank with the Three.

decisions.choice: to the Three he did not come: he did not reach their rank
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:19. "Come to" means to attain to or be counted with. The same is said of Benaiah in verse 25.

decisions.choice: given more honor
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that he was honored more, without the uncertain "doubly"; the sense is the same as Literal and Balanced.

records.source: בְּנָיָ֨ה בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֧ע בֶּן־אִֽישׁ־חַ֛יִל רַב־פְּעָלִ֖ים מִֽן־קַבְצְאֵ֑ל ה֣וּא הִכָּ֗ה אֵ֣ת שְׁנֵ֤י אֲרִיאֵל֙ מוֹאָ֔ב וְ֠הוּא יָרַ֞ד וְהִכָּ֧ה אֶֽת־הָאֲרִ֛י בְּת֥וֹךְ הַבּ֖וֹר בְּי֥וֹם הַשָּֽׁלֶג׃
records.gloss: Benaiah son of Jehoiada [was a] son of a man of valor, great of deeds, from Kabzeel; he struck down [the] two ariel of Moab; and he went down and struck down the lion in [the] middle of the pit on [the] day of the snow.
pieces: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a brave man from Kabzeel who did great deeds. He struck down the two champions of Moab. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.

L.22: Benaiah son of Jehoiada [was the] son of a man of valor, great of deeds, from Kabzeel. He struck down the two champions of Moab; and he went down and struck down the lion in [the] middle of the pit on the day of the snow.

R.22: Benaiah son of Jehoiada came from Kabzeel. He was the son of a brave man who had done great things. Benaiah killed the two greatest fighters of Moab. And one day when there was snow on the ground, he went down into a pit and killed a lion there.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:20, word for word
decisions.reason: Chronicles has the same words. It writes "a man of valor" plainly, where the written text of Samuel has "a living man", and spells "lion" with a shorter form of the word.

decisions.choice: the two champions of Moab: the sense of "ariel" is uncertain
alternatives: the two sons of Ariel of Moab
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:20, the word may mean "lion of God", a title for a great warrior, and that is how it is taken here; the Greek translation reads it as a person's name, Ariel.

decisions.choice: Benaiah son of Jehoiada: commander of David's guard
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:20. Benaiah was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites (18:17) and later commanded Solomon's army (1 Kings 2:35).

decisions.choice: champions (Balanced); greatest fighters (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:20.

records.source: וְהֽוּא־הִכָּה֩ אֶת־הָאִ֨ישׁ הַמִּצְרִ֜י אִ֥ישׁ מִדָּ֣ה׀חָמֵ֣שׁ בָּאַמָּ֗ה וּבְיַ֨ד הַמִּצְרִ֤י חֲנִית֙ כִּמְנ֣וֹר אֹרְגִ֔ים וַיֵּ֥רֶד אֵלָ֖יו בַּשָּׁ֑בֶט וַיִּגְזֹ֤ל אֶֽת־הַחֲנִית֙ מִיַּ֣ד הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַיַּהַרְגֵ֖הוּ בַּחֲנִיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he struck down the man the Egyptian, a man of stature, five by the cubit; and in [the] hand of the Egyptian [was] a spear like a beam of weavers; and he went down to him with the staff and seized the spear from [the] hand of the Egyptian and killed him with his [own] spear.
pieces: He also struck down an Egyptian, a man of great height, {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} tall. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand like a weaver's beam, but Benaiah went down against him with a club, snatched the spear from the Egyptian's grip and killed him with his own weapon.

L.23: And he struck down the Egyptian man, a man of stature, five cubits [tall]; and in the hand of the Egyptian [was] a spear like a weavers' beam, but he went down to him with a staff and snatched the spear from the hand of the Egyptian and killed him with his own spear.

R.23: He also killed an Egyptian who was a huge man, {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} tall. The Egyptian held a spear as big as the heavy beam of a weaver's loom, but Benaiah went to fight him with only a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with it.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:21, with the Egyptian's height and a spear like a weaver's beam
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 23:21 calls the Egyptian "a man of appearance". Chronicles says he was a man of stature, five cubits tall, and that his spear was like a weaver's beam, the words used of Goliath's spear (1 Samuel 17:7; 2 Samuel 21:19). Otherwise the verse follows Samuel.

decisions.choice: five cubits; a weaver's beam: a giant with a huge spear
decisions.reason: A cubit was the length from elbow to fingertip, about 18 inches, so five cubits is about 7 1/2 feet. A weaver's beam was the thick rod of a loom; the comparison describes the spear's heavy shaft.

decisions.choice: with a staff ... with his own spear: the champion is killed by his own weapon
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:21. Benaiah came against an armed man with only a club, took his spear and killed him with it, as David killed Goliath with Goliath's own sword (1 Samuel 17:51).

decisions.choice: a man of great height, a huge man; club; the heavy beam of a weaver's loom (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "a man of stature" means. The staff is the ordinary word for a rod or club, as in 2 Samuel 23:21, and Readable explains the weaver's beam as in 1 Samuel 17:7.
